question: Behind the cornea, there is a dark muscular structure called the ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**iris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Behind the cornea, there is a dark muscular structure called the **Iris**. 
 
• It is a thin annular structure of the eye.
 
• Iris is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil and thus controlling the light that enters the eye.​
 
• Layers__
 __
 
• Iris consists of two layers
 
• In front, a pigmented fibrovascular layer known as stroma
 
• A layer of pigmented epithelial cells beneath the stroma.
 
• The stroma is connected to a sphincter muscle.
 
 
 
• Iris:
 
 
• The coloured ring around the pupil of the eye is called the iris.
 
• Controls light levels inside the eye.
 
• Tiny muscles that dilate and constrict the pupil size.
 
• Divides the front of the eye from the back of the eye.
 
• Colour comes from melanin.
 
• Iris is a part of Sclerotic and choroid. 
 
 
 
• Zones__
 
 
• Pupillary zone
 
• Ciliary zone
